She came down to the flats with the light still thin and the bucket cold against her hip. Low tide had opened the whole silver mile of it, ribbed mud and standing water, and the channel markers showed the way they always did, one after another into the gray.

Tobin's wrench was still on the shelf in the pump house; she could see the door standing shut and bolted, the way she'd left it after the storm. Good. One thing in the world stayed where you put it.

The digging went slow and she didn't mind. Bring patience, get clams. The heron had its spot at the channel edge and she had hers, and between them the morning divided itself fairly. By full light the bucket was heavy enough to make her back complain, and she told it, as always, to file its complaint with the management.
